claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys have high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys exhibit coercive fields below approximately 100 Oe.
Controlled intermediate-temperature aging followed by rapid quenching can induce nanoscale ordered precipitates in an fcc FeCoNi-based alloy.
An optimized aging window can produce partial precipitation while retaining an overall fcc matrix.
The induced nanoscale ordered precipitates will be dispersed within the fcc matrix.
The nanoscale ordered precipitates will have higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the surrounding matrix.
The nanoscale ordered precipitates will act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Pinning by the precipitates will impede magnetic domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion will increase the energy barrier for domain reversal.
The increased domain-reversal barrier will raise the coercive field.
The aged alloy will have a room-temperature coercive field above approximately 100 Oe and greater than that of an untreated matched sample.
The aging treatment will largely preserve the alloy's high saturation magnetization.
The proposed intervention is applicable to near-equiatomic FeCoNi compositions.
Avoiding complete phase transformation, coarse precipitates, and extensive grain growth requires precise control of aging parameters.
